history.period: Present structure built 1944; origins are legendary
history.summary: Famous Shakti shrine on an island in the middle of the Nandini river. Legend: the demon Arunasura, protected by Brahma's boon (no death by two- or four-legged beings) and armed with the Gayatri mantra, was tricked by the Goddess as Mohini, then stung to death by a swarm of bees when she hid in a rock — Devi as Bhramari. Sage Jabali, unable to complete his yajna during a drought, cursed the divine cow Nandini to flow as a river; promised relief when the Goddess would manifest as a linga in her waters. 'Kateel' = Kati (waist/centre) + Ila (earth): the centre of the Nandini. The present structure dates to 1944; the old temple is said to have been washed away in floods. The temple runs six traditional Yakshagana troupes (Kateel Melas). CSV correction: the temple is at Kateel town, NOT Mangalore — Kateel is a separate temple town ~26-30 km from Mangaluru. Opening-hour sources conflict on the morning start (4:00 vs 5:30 vs 6:00 AM); verify before visiting.

name: Kateel Shri Durgaparameshwari Temple
town_description: Kateel is a temple town in Dakshina Kannada district, Karnataka, about 26-30 km from Mangaluru, built around the Durgaparameshwari temple that stands on an island in the Nandini river. The name derives from 'Kati' (waist/centre) + 'Ila' (earth).

travel.road: Well connected by road/bus from Mangaluru (~30 km, 45-60 minutes)

visitor_information.best_time: During Navratri for the festival experience; otherwise October-March is the most comfortable season for coastal Karnataka.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 5:30 AM - 9:30 PM daily (Friday till ~10:30 PM); a Karnataka-government study says 6:00 AM - 9:30 PM. Sources conflict on the morning start time (4:00 vs 5:30 vs 6:00 AM) — verify before visiting.
